title: AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 Series embedded processors offer up to 256 Zen 6c cores, PCIe Gen 6, and CXL 3.1
summary:
AMD has introduced the EPYC Embedded 9006 Series SP7, a family of high-performance x86 SoCs built around the Zen 6 and Zen 6c architectures using a 2nm CPU process. Designed for semiconductor automated test equipment (ATE), networking appliances, firewalls, and enterprise storage controllers, the new embedded processors feature up to 256 cores, 512 threads, and 1GB of L3 cache, with power ratings ranging from 400W to 600W. Compared to the previous-generation EPYC Embedded 9005 Series, the new processors offer 16-channel DDR5 memory with RDIMM and MRDIMM support, up to 96 PCIe Gen 6 lanes, and CXL 3.1 connectivity. They also offer improved security, enterprise-class reliability, and seven-year product availability, making them suitable for long-lifecycle embedded systems. summary:

The SDR part is implemented through an RTL2832U+R860 combo supporting 100 kHz to 1.74 GHz frequency and 100 kHz-28.8 MHz HF direct sampling.  The HAT also features a Semtech SX1262 LoRa transceiver supporting the 860-960 MHz frequency band, 22 dBm max output power, and Meshtastic firmware. summary:
ANAVI I2C TPM 2.0 is an open-source hardware I2C TPM 2.0 security module for Raspberry Pi single board computers based on the Infineon Optiga SLB 9673 TPM 2.0 chip. It’s an alternative to the earlier ANAVI TPM 2.0 module using an Optiga SLB 9672 SPI chip. The add-on board is designed for developers, hobbyists, and professionals who require enhanced security for Raspberry Pi-based projects. summary:
The Bluetooth SIG ratified the Bluetooth 7.0 specification on November 3, 2026, with the highlight of the new Bluetooth Core specification being optional support for HDT (High Data Throughput), delivering up to 7.5 Mbps bitrate. We first covered HDT in 2025 when initial/early support was implemented into the Ceva-Waves Links200 multi-protocol platform IP, and followed last September with the Realtek RTL8773J Bluetooth 7-ready Cortex-M55/M33 microcontroller. The main news is that the specification for Bluetooth 7.0 and the associated HDT feature is officially ratified/adopted. Bluetooth 7.0 highlights: Bluetooth High Data Throughput (HDT) introduces a new Bluetooth LE physical layer that increases the maximum Bluetooth bit rate to 7.5 Mbps while improving wireless efficiency and robustness. The higher bitrate is enabled by a combination of higher-order modulation, convolutional forward error correction, synchronization enhancements, adaptive rate selection, and enhanced packet architectures. It will be especially useful for high-resolution and lossless audio streaming. Bluetooth [...]
